Imagine a new startup develops a revolutionary supercomputer that has immense processing power but does not use an operating system. Instead, every user must manually control the hardware, load programs, and manage memory allocation themselves. One day, a researcher runs an advanced AI model while another team member tries to access stored data, and a third team attempts to install a new application. Soon, conflicts arise—files get corrupted, the system crashes frequently, and tasks run inconsistently due to manual intervention. Given this scenario, explain the challenges faced without an operating system and how an OS can resolve these issues by managing processes, memory, and hardware interactions.
a) Define an Operating System. Give two examples. (5 Marks)
OR List and explain any two basic operations of an operating system. (5 Marks)

Five philosophers are sitting around a circular dining table, enjoying their meals. However, to eat, each philosopher needs two chopsticks—one on their left and one on their right. The problem is that there are only five chopsticks, and if all philosophers pick up just one chopstick at the same time, they might end up waiting indefinitely (deadlock) or some may starve while others keep eating. To solve this, they decide to follow a set of rules using semaphores to ensure that no two neighbouring philosophers pick up chopsticks at the same time, allowing everyone to eat without conflicts. Present this strategy and discuss it in detail.
